questions.q_en: If A*B means A is the mother of B; A@B means A is the father of B; A!B means A is the son of B; A~B means A is the daughter of B; A^B means A is the brother of B; A:B means A is the sister of B; A/B means A is the wife of B. In the given expression, S@T!U:V?W, if T is grandson of W then which of the following symbol will replace the question mark?
questions.solution_en:
A*B means A is the mother of B.

A@B means A is the father of B.

A!B means A is the son of B.

A~B means A is the daughter of B.

A^B means A is the brother of B.

A:B means A is the sister of B.

A/B means A is the wife of B.

S@T!U:V?W

S is the father of T.

T is the son of U.

U is the sister of V.

T is grandson of W.

So, V should be son/daughter of W.

Therefore, V!W or V~W.

questions.q_en: If 15 January 1997 is Wednesday, then what will be the day of the week on 5 January 2000?
questions.solution_en:
15 January 1997 was Wednesday.

Total number of days from 15 January 1997 to 15 January 2000 = 3 years = 3 * 365 = 1095 days

Total number of days from 15 January 1997 to 5 January 2000 = 1095 - 10 = 1085 days

1085 days = 155 weeks

Which means the day on 15 January 1997 and 5 January 2000 will be same and it is Wednesday.
questions.solution_hi:
15 January 1997 was Wednesday.

Total number of days from 15 January 1997 to 5 January 2000 = 1095 - 10 = 1085 days

1085 days = 155 weeks

Which means the day on 15 January 1997 and 5 January 2000 will be same and it is Wednesday.

questions.q_en:
Given below is a statement followed by two possible reasons numbered I and II. Read the statement carefully and decide which of the two explain(s) the event/observation/information given in the statement.

statement:

In India, large cities have attracted migrant population from across rural parts of the country. According to 2011 census, in India's six largest metros (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Hyderabad), approximately 48% of the residents were migrants.

reasons:

I) Migration happens due to availability of better career and economic prospects in cities.

II) Migration happens because people like travelling and exploring new cities.
options_en: Neither I nor II is a possible reason.
Only I is a possible reason.
Only II is a possible reason.
Both I and II are possible reasons.
questions.solution_en:
The statement mentions that large cities in India have attracted a significant migrant population from rural areas, and approximately 48% of the residents in the six largest metros are migrants according to the 2011 census.

I: The people are moving to cities because they perceive better career and economic opportunities there. Economic factors, such as job availability, higher wages, and improved livelihoods, become the primary drivers of migration.

The migration happens because people like traveling and exploring new cities, is not supported by the statement.

So, only I is a possible reason.

questions.q_en:
Two statements numbered I and II are given below. You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question.

There are five friends A, B, C, D and E standing in different directions with respect to each other. Towards which direction is Person D with respect to Person B?

I. Person C is to the east of person D and to the north of person E, who is to the north of person B.

II. Person D is to the north of person A, who is to the east of person E. Person E is to the west of person B.
options_en: If the data in statement I alone are sufficient to answer the question while the data in statement II alone are not sufficient to answer the question
If the data in both the statements I and II together are not sufficient to answer the question
If the data either in statement I or Statement II alone are sufficient to answer the question
If the data in both statements I and II together are necessary to answer the question
questions.solution_en:
Only statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question.

Detailed solution

Using Statement I alone:

I. Person C is to the east of person D and to the north of person E, who is to the North of person B.

So, Person D is in North-west direction with respect to B.

Using Statement II alone:

II. Person D is to the north of person A, who is to the east of person E. Person E is to the west of person B.

So, there are two possible cases i.e. Case 1 and Case 2.

So, the direction of person D with respect to person B is not known.
